title: Validating conversation keywords against attitudes, with a no-chat arm and delayed follow-up
rationale: In the source study both arms chatted, so the 0.64-point shift (95% CI [0.37, 0.91]) cannot be split between the op-ed and the chatbot. Keyword gaps of 16.6 and 26.7 percentage points may reflect echoing of the op-ed rather than changed belief, and attitudes were measured only once, right after exposure.
contribution: Identifies the chatbot's added effect beyond the op-ed text, checks whether keyword use tracks real attitude change, and tests whether the effect lasts.
limitations: Wave 2 attrition may be differential across arms.
Keyword dictionary from the source study is not available in the survey text and must be supplied.
Pre-measurement may sensitise participants and inflate consistency.
US online panel only; anti-spending group may again be small.

design.title: Op-ed x chatbot factorial with pre/post and 2-week follow-up
design.overview: Participants report their spending attitude and certainty, are randomised to one of four arms (op-ed or placebo article, followed by a chatbot conversation or no conversation), and then report attitude and certainty again. About two weeks later they complete the same measures. Chat transcripts are coded with the existing keyword dictionary and by blinded human or LLM raters for argument adoption versus echo.
design.hypothesis: If conversation adds persuasion beyond the text, the op-ed+chat arm will shift attitudes more than the op-ed-only arm, and the difference will persist at 2 weeks. If it does not, the arms will not differ, or the chat-driven difference will fade. Within the op-ed+chat arm, argument-adoption coding should predict attitude shift better than keyword counts.
design.primaryOutcome: Immediate change in support toward the op-ed position (post minus pre), with the 2-week change as the durability outcome.
design.comparison: Op-ed+chatbot versus op-ed only (chatbot increment); op-ed versus placebo (text effect); wave 2 versus wave 1 change; keyword and adoption measures as predictors of shift within the op-ed+chat arm.
design.population: US online panel adults who hold a position on government spending, about 400 per arm (1,600 total before attrition).

questions.text: You are invited to a research study on opinions about government spending. It has two parts, about two weeks apart. Participation is voluntary. Do you consent to take part?
Overall, how much do you support increased government spending on social programs? (1 = strongly oppose, 7 = strongly support)
How certain are you of your position? (0-100)
Please read this article carefully. It argues against your stated position on government spending. [The op-ed text matching the participant's pre-measured position is shown here.]
Please read this article carefully. It is about an unrelated everyday topic. [The placebo article text is shown here.]
Now please talk with our chatbot for about 3 minutes. It will ask what you thought of the article you just read. Type your thoughts and respond to its questions.
Overall, how much do you support increased government spending on social programs? (1 = strongly oppose, 7 = strongly support)
How certain are you of your position? (0-100)
Overall, how much do you support increased government spending on social programs? (1 = strongly oppose, 7 = strongly support)
How certain are you of your position? (0-100)

Thank you. This study examined how reading an article and chatting with a chatbot affect opinions. The op-ed presented one side of a debated issue and the other article was unrelated. Please contact the research team with any questions.

assumptions: Power: about 215 per arm detects 0.4 SD at 80% power (source H1 MDE 0.3985 at 224/215 per arm; observed 0.638). The chat increment is likely smaller than the full effect, so target about 400 per arm (1,600 total), inflated for wave 2 attrition.
Online panel platform; wave 2 invitation sent about 14 days after wave 1.
Keywords coded with the source dictionary plus blinded human or LLM coding of argument adoption versus echo, with a validated subsample.
Mediation by keyword use is exploratory and observational within the op-ed+chat arm.
Primary analysis is OLS on change scores with robust SEs, preregistered.
unresolved: Op-ed and placebo article texts, chatbot configuration and keyword dictionary must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation, including the wave 2 bonus, must be supplied.
Wave 2 is fielded as a separate session; the flow here lists it in sequence.
